comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's current programme page, checked 2026-10-03, describes a three-year Applied Physics bachelor organised around classical mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism and quantum mechanics, with one physics course, one mathematics course and a laboratory or project in each quarter of year one and two theory courses plus a laboratory or project in each quarter of year two. Its linked official curriculum chart was created in August 2026 and is marked September 2026. The chart supplies the course-level allocation of the complete 180-EC programme. Year three contains a 30-EC minor, two 5-EC electives, 5 EC of Critical Reflection on Science and Argumentation, and a 15-EC individual Bachelor Final Project.

programmes.label: Bachelor Applied Physics at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: Applied Physics is a cumulative physics-and-engineering degree whose compulsory spine combines classical and advanced mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, waves, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, transport phenomena and solid-state physics with analysis, linear algebra, differential equations, Fourier methods, probability, computational science, systems and signals, circuits, electronics, instrumentation, three design courses, three laboratory courses and a 15-EC individual physics research project. UCR offers a useful mathematics and computational-modelling sequence and two broad sustainability gateways that touch on selected physical concepts. It does not offer the required university-level physics core, experimental-physics laboratory and measurement progression, electronic instrumentation, materials and quantum sequence, or comparable applied-physics research environment. A UCR pathway could study mathematical modelling and technology in an interdisciplinary way, but it would not be a defensible Applied Physics comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official September 2026 curriculum chart accounts for the full 180 EC. Year one totals 60 EC across mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, waves, four mathematics courses, two introductory laboratories and two design-engineering courses. Year two totals 60 EC across advanced mechanics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, systems and signals, physical transport phenomena, solid-state physics, advanced linear algebra and differential equations, circuits/electronics/instrumentation, computational science, a research laboratory, physics design and technology management. Year three totals 60 EC through a 30-EC minor, two 5-EC electives, 5 EC of critical reflection on science and argumentation, and a 15-EC individual Bachelor Final Project. The live programme page confirms that the programme's four core themes are classical mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism and quantum mechanics, and that practical or project work accompanies the physics and mathematics progression.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide meaningful mathematical foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science add computational foundations, while DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision offers general digital image analysis. ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I surveys selected concepts from physics, chemistry and materials science in a sustainability context, and ENSGATE201 Sustainability Essentials II includes broad work on waves, chemistry and materials. The workbook nevertheless contains no dedicated classical mechanics, advanced mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, optics, wave physics, physical transport phenomena, solid-state physics, atomic or materials physics, circuits and electronics, scientific instrumentation, experimental-physics methods, precision measurement, or cumulative physics laboratory sequence. DISMATH312 studies mathematical systems, differential equations and signal representations rather than physical electronics and measurement hardware; DISDATA212 studies digital image-processing algorithms rather than imaging physics or instrument design; and the sustainability gateways introduce selected concepts for environmental study rather than forming a physics sequence. UCR also lacks TU Delft's three staged physics-design courses, second-year research laboratory and 15-EC individual applied-physics research project. The closest possible 24-course UCR combination would therefore be a mathematical and sustainability-oriented liberal-arts pathway with the target programme's defining physical theory, experimentation and engineering formation absent.
